pr_title: Requires replace should not error on missing index steps
pr_body:
RequiresReplace paths with IndexSteps that have been added or removed will fail to apply against one or the other state values. We were previously ignoring the error from apply the path to the `priorVal`, but this can happen in either direction.

Only fail if both values produce an error. In the case of a single error, make sure the other value is a valid Null of the correct type.

Fixes #20294

issue_context.title: Requires replacement on removed list block
issue_context.body:
If an attribute within a list block requires replacement, and the block is removed from the config, the path to the attribute triggering the replacement can't be applied to the new state. The paths are constructed based on the prior state, so this results in an error like:

        Error: Provider produced invalid plan

        Provider "aws" has indicated "requires replacement" on
        aws_batch_job_definition.test for a non-existent attribute path
        cty.Path{cty.GetAttrStep{Name:"retry_strategy"},
        cty.IndexStep{Key:cty.NumberIntVal(0)}, cty.GetAttrStep{Name:"attempts"}}.

review_comments:
In the case where the thing being changed contains `cty.DynamicPseudoType` attributes in its schema it is possible for the prior and planned to actually _not_ have the same type (contradicting the comment that used to be here, which was incorrect for a number of reasons :confounded: )

In think in this context it doesn't actually matter, since we're only using these values to run `Equals` below and that'll never show a null as equal to a non-null anyway, but maybe it's worth noting here in a comment that it's generally more correct to use the schema's implied type to create a null but we're intentionally not doing that here because we know it's safe. I worry that a future reader may see this and think it a good general usage example to copy elsewhere, in situations where the exact type of null may be important.

Ah yes, that was intended here, since It was only for the comparison and I didn't want to traverse the schema to check for a dynamic type. I'll add the comment for our future selves so we don't rely on the type.
